entities.desc: YANKEE BLUE is the allegation that the US Air Force ran a fake UFO reverse-engineering programme on its own personnel — briefing officers in classified units into believing they had been read on to a recovery effort, using fabricated material, as a counterintelligence or hazing exercise. If documented it would be the strongest single item in the coverup strand, because it is the government generating false UAP belief inside its own ranks. It is not documented. Two FOIA cases have returned negative: OSD case 25-F-3514 (September 2025) reported no responsive records after searches of the electronic and paper holdings, and AFOSI case 2025-06002-F reported no investigative reports, summaries or closure memoranda. On 1 October 2025 Pentagon spokesperson Susan Gough stated she could not confirm the alleged memorandum. The Department reportedly reopened the search in December 2025 with no published result. The programme is retained on the board at Tier B with the allegation graded Tier 3 and the negative FOIA findings graded Tier 1. A negative primary finding is itself a documented fact and belongs on a board about concealment — but it is a finding about the absence of a record, not a record.

The company's own 1956 publication carries a signed statement attributed to 'General of the Army Douglas MacArthur, Chairman of the Board, Sperry Rand Corporation', and a New York Journal-American column of 17 January 1957, preserved in CIA records, reports that 'Gen. B. Montgomery at General Electric. Thirteen further instances of the general-officer-to-prime-contractor movement, in one citable contemporaneous document held by CIA.

Two corrections travel with it. The company was not called Sperry Rand in 1986: it had been Sperry Corporation since 1979, and it was Sperry Corporation that Burroughs absorbed. SEC's own record shows CIK 0000746838 changing its conformed name from BURROUGHS CORP /DE/ on 4 December 1986, and Unisys carrying Sperry's obligations thereafter, including its sale of the Sperry Aerospace Group that same month. entities.desc: The Air Technical Intelligence Center, established in 1951 out of the Air Materiel Command intelligence organisation (T-2) at Wright Field, was the United States' centre for the exploitation of foreign aerospace technology. It was the organisation that processed the Operation Paperclip haul, that dismantled and reverse-engineered captured Soviet and German airframes, and that was institutionally designed to answer exactly one question: what is this thing and how does it work. Every official UFO project of the legacy era — SIGN, GRUDGE and Blue Book — was hosted here, which is a fact usually reported as an administrative detail and is in fact the central structural point of this domain. The United States did not assign unidentified flying objects to a science agency, an academic body or an air-defence command; it assigned them to the shop that takes recovered hardware apart. The Air Force organizational-history record gives a discontinuation and a new constitution rather than a renaming: the Air Technical Intelligence Center was redesignated Aerospace Technical Intelligence Center on 21 September 1959 and discontinued on 1 July 1961, and the Foreign Technology Division was constituted, activated and organized the same day, absorbing the mission and resources; FTD's own later name is the National Air and Space Intelligence Center, which remains at Wright-Patterson today. It also issued Blue Book Special Report No. 14 in 1955 and was the terminal analytical node under AFR 200-2. If a legacy recovery and exploitation effort existed, ATIC and its successors are the institutional address, and its 1947-1951 T-2 intelligence files have never been subject to a comprehensive declassification review.

entities.desc: The SAPOC was established on 5 January 1994, not in 2010. A Deputy Secretary of Defense information bulletin of November 1994 records that 'On January 5th, 1994, the Deputy Secretary of Defense (DEPSECDEF) significantly enhanced changes in the DoD Special Access Program (SAP) management and control structures' and that the plan 'standardized and formalized the SAP approval, termination, revalidation and restructuring process through the Special Access Program Oversight Committee (SAPOC). A Senior Review Group (SRG) was established to support the SAPOC principals'; the Joint Security Commission called it a 'recent formation' on 28 February 1994. DoD Directive 5205.07 of 1 July 2010 is therefore a later instrument that re-established a committee which had been running for sixteen years, and it survives in the 12 September 2024 reissue as 'the senior governing body of the DoD SAP Enterprise'. Under the 2013 instruction its chair is the Deputy Secretary of Defense, its vice-chair the Under Secretary of Defense for Acquisition, Technology and Logistics, and its executive secretary the Director of DoD SAPCO; its general membership is the Under Secretaries for Policy, Comptroller/CFO, Intelligence, and Personnel and Readiness, the Vice Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, the DoD Chief Information Officer, the General Counsel of the Department, the Director of Cost Assessment and Program Evaluation, the Under Secretaries of the Army, Navy and Air Force, the Vice Chiefs of Staff of the Army and Air Force, the Vice Chief of Naval Operations and the Assistant Commandant of the Marine Corps. Its three primary functions are to review issues on which the Senior Review Group could not reach unanimity, to ensure combatant command warfighting needs are reflected in SAP programmatics and budgets, and - the function that matters here - to 'Conduct an annual review and validation of SAP reports sent to the Congressional defense and intelligence committees'.
